title: Audit event classification and actor-context hints for RBACv2 SSO changes
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Goal: Define a pragmatic, searchable, and storage-efficient classification for audit events produced by RBACv2 and SSO/SAML admin flows. This ticket covers what to log for admin-driven changes (role grants/revokes, policy edits, SSO mapping changes), how to represent actor and target context so downstream tools (Console, Investigations, Alerts) can quickly answer: who changed what, why, and what actually changed. We want a lightweight set of fields + optional compact delta that balances fidelity and retention cost. This is scoped to the control-plane audit pipeline (ingest -> transform -> storage), not the UI surface.
background: Current audit events are inconsistent: sometimes full object snapshots, sometimes freeform messages. RBACv2 introduces richer objects (roles, bindings, conditions) and SSO introduces external identity mappings. We need a consistent contract so search, alerting, and retention policies can operate reliably without exploding storage costs.
acceptance_criteria: A clear event classification taxonomy (e.g., Authorization.Change, Authorization.Grant, Authorization.Revoke, Identity.Mapping.Change, SSO.AuthFlow) documented and accepted by Sec/Platform.
Actor and target semantics defined: actor.id, actor.type, actor.auth_source, target.id, target.type, target.resource_path.
A compact change representation: optional 'delta' string (compact patch) and an explicit 'intent' field that encodes admin intent (e.g., 'grant-role', 'rollback', 'emergency-disable').
Examples covering common RBACv2 workflows (role create/update/delete, binding change, condition edit) and SSO mapping updates included as samples.

Implementation design doc and schema samples merged to shared Confluence and linked from this ticket; at least one end-to-end test in audit pipeline that asserts classification and required fields are present.
Storage/retention recommendation: full snapshots retained for high-impact events for 365 days; compact deltas for medium-impact events for 90 days; low-impact telemetry for 30 days.
proposed_schema_samples:
{
  "event_id": "uuid",
  "timestamp": "ISO-8601",
  "classification": "Identity.Mapping.Change",
  "intent": "sso-map-update",
  "actor.id": "svc:automation",
  "actor.type": "service",
  "actor.auth_source": "ci",
  "target.id": "sso-mapping:okta->redwood",
  "target.type": "sso_mapping",
  "delta": "map(group:eng)->role:engineer",
  "context": "api",
  "outcome": "partial_failure",
  "note": "Reconciler applied subset of mappings due to filter"
}
implementation_notes: In the transform stage we will normalize incoming events into a flat key namespace to avoid nested lookups in OLAP storage (avoid JSON blobs where possible). Use dotted keys as string names (e.g., 'actor.id').

Delta representation: prefer a single-line compact patch string using a small grammar (+ for adds, - for removes, ~ for replaces). Avoid full JSON patches in hot paths. Store full snapshots only for events classified as 'high' impact.
Add classification header early in pipeline so downstream retention and alerting can make fast decisions without materializing full event.
Map SSO principals to canonical actor ids at ingestion time when possible; when mapping fails, emit actor.auth_source and original_principal fields.
Provide a compatibility shim for older events: a migration transform will add classification and best-effort actor.target fields for the next 90 days.
Expose new fields in Console search and Investigation API; add filters for classification and intent.
Coordinate with Compliance team to validate retention tiers for PII-sensitive fields (e.g., original_principal).
testing_plan: Unit tests for transform logic including classification heuristics (rule set and precedence).
Integration test that emits an RBACv2 role-change event, verifies transformed record contains required keys and correct classification.
Chaos test that simulates partial failures in SSO mapping to assert actor.auth_source and original_principal are emitted.
E2E smoke test that ensures Console can filter by classification and intent without extra indexing changes.
